key_insight: Powder-in-tube mechanical confinement turns brittle Heusler caloric powders into fatigue-resistant composites by preventing catastrophic fragmentation and enabling load transfer under cyclic stress.
engineering_relevance: This design principle could make magneto- and elastocaloric cooling materials durable enough for repeated operation in real devices, despite intrinsic brittleness.
method: Embed Heusler alloy powder in a ductile steel tube with ~87% packing density.
Apply cyclic loading while measuring strain and AC magnetic susceptibility simultaneously in situ.
Use the composite sheath to confine damage and sustain load transfer between particles.
evidence_signal: The composites survived 100,000 load cycles at 250 MPa without structural failure and withstood overload stresses up to 700 MPa.
watch_item: Macroscopic strain does not directly reflect the transforming phase fraction because the internal stress field is highly heterogeneous, so mechanical readouts alone can be misleading.
paper_title: Powder-in-tube confinement as a design principle for fatigue-resistant caloric materials
